name: AlternatingCaseShift
idea: A simple, highly deterministic character-by-character substitution cipher designed to be extremely easy for LLMs to reason about. It shifts uppercase letters forward by 3 positions in the alphabet (A->D, B->E, ..., Z->C) and lowercase letters backward by 3 positions (a->x, b->y, ..., z->w). Numbers, spaces, and punctuation marks remain completely unchanged.
encrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it forward by 3 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around from Z to A). Formula: new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 65 + 3) % 26) + 65)
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it backward by 3 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around from a to z). Formula: new_char = chr(((ord(char) - 97 - 3) % 26) + 97)
3. If it is any other character (numbers, spaces, punctuation, symbols), leave it completely unchanged.
decrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it backward by 3 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around from A to Z). Formula: original_char = chr(((ord(char) - 65 - 3) % 26) + 65)
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it forward by 3 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around from z to a). Formula: original_char = chr(((ord(char) - 97 + 3) % 26) + 97)
3. If it is any other character (numbers, spaces, punctuation, symbols), leave it completely unchanged.
